close_reason: Updated all six Err(_) arms in malformed-DER lint reporting to bind the der::Error value and include it in the LintResult detail string via Display interpolation: rfc5280.rs (BasicConstraints, ExtendedKeyUsage), rfc6125.rs (SubjectAltName), rfc8398.rs (two SubjectAltName sites), rfc8551.rs (ExtendedKeyUsage). The detail strings now carry the failing tag, offset, expected vs. found, and sub-component path that der::Error provides via Display, which is valuable in the audit trail when a customer ticket reports 'malformed DER' on a real cert. No new tests: the malformed-DER path has no existing coverage (no synthesized malformed-extension fixtures in the workspace), and constructing one principled-enough to oracle would require either der::Any manipulation or a hand-crafted DER blob — out of scope for an idiom fix. All 129 lib tests + 7 doc tests pass; clippy --all-features clean.
description: Across rfc5280.rs:280,375, rfc6125.rs:123, rfc8398.rs:120,259,277, and rfc8551.rs:121, the pattern `Err(_) => LintResult::error("...malformed DER")` discards the `der::Error` value returned by x509-cert's `from_der` parsers. der::Error carries structured info (failing tag, offset, expected vs. found, sub-component path) that would be valuable in the audit trail when a lint reports 'malformed DER' on a real cert in a customer ticket. Idiomatic Rust folds the error into the message via Display: `Err(e) => LintResult::error(format!("BasicConstraints extension value is malformed DER: {e}"))` or a structured variant. The current pattern is the error-handling antipattern flagged by the review-rusty error-handling section: 'error variants that wrap String for the message instead of structured fields' — except worse, because the structured info exists at the call site and is actively thrown away. Fix: every `Err(_)` arm in malformed-DER lint reporting should bind the error and include it in the LintResult detail string (or, if the cost of carrying it is too high, document the discard in a comment explaining why).
title: DER parse errors discarded via Err(_) lose structured error info from der::Error
